Front: What changes during training but not ordinary inference?
Back: Training updates model parameters; ordinary inference uses fixed parameters. §1.2, p. 5

Front: Does adding a definition to a prompt update model weights?
Back: No. It changes the available context, not the model parameters. §1.2, p. 5

Front: How are tokens different from words?
Back: Tokens may be words, word parts, punctuation, or spaces; segmentation depends on the tokenizer. §1.3, p. 6

Front: How does a token ID differ from its embedding?
Back: An ID indexes the vocabulary; an embedding is a learned numerical vector. §1.4, pp. 7–8
A position cannot access future tokens; it can use earlier and currently available tokens. §1.5, p. 9

Front: What roles do queries, keys, and values play?
Back: Queries match keys; normalized scores weight values from permitted positions. §1.5, p. 9

Front: What happens when temperature increases at fixed logits?
Back: Probabilities become less concentrated, without changing token ranking or adding knowledge. §1.6, p. 10

Front: Does a token's 80% probability mean an answer is 80% true?
Back: No. It measures next-token probability given the context and model, not truth. §§1.6, 1.8, pp. 10, 15

Front: How does RAG provide information without retraining?
Back: It retrieves external passages and supplies them as context while model parameters remain fixed. §1.7, p. 14

Front: How can you test an AI-generated explanation?
Back: Use independent explanations, controlled comparisons, and error-detecting checks. §§1.8–1.10, pp. 14–17
